source: Young, J.R. 2012. 'SMART BIOSECURITY: A Planning and Education Tool for Smallholder Farmers' -- description for trainers plus the 16-point SMART BIOSECURITY planning tool, ACIAR/USYD (mekonglivestock.wordpress.com)
text: SMART BIOSECURITY is a simple, self-directed planning tool designed for a farmer to work through with their local Animal Health Worker: the farmer estimates their own livestock's healthy value versus its value if diseased (plus treatment and other costs), calculating a rough 'cost of disease' figure, then works through a checklist of 16 low-cost biosecurity practices (the acronym S-M-A-R-T B-I-O-S-E-C-U-R-I-T-Y), each carrying a simple point score reflecting its relative protective value: Segregation of animals including water sources (2 points) -- fencing, tethering, or natural boundaries to limit animal-to-animal contact; Manure control (1 point) -- collecting and removing manure from animal areas; Avoid animal movement and mixing (3 points) -- especially at communal grazing areas, since infected animals may show no visible signs; Record keeping (1 point) -- of treatments, disease cases, breeding dates, and vaccination dates for correct boosters; Traders kept off farm property (3 points) -- met at the road or village gate instead, since traders visit many farms and can carry disease on clothing/shoes; Boundaries and borders (2 points) -- agreed with neighbours to limit animal mixing; Immunise with vaccination (3 points) -- planned together with the local animal health worker, not relied on alone; Outbreak awareness (2 points) -- staying informed of local disease status and raising vigilance during outbreaks; Signage for awareness (1 point) -- simple signs such as 'Traders please wait at gate'; Enquire of health of bull and breeding matches (2 points) -- only using breeding animals with a clean disease and vaccination history; Cleaning of at-risk materials (2 points) -- removing organic material from equipment, clothing, shoes, and hands; Use disinfectants after cleaning (2 points) -- since disinfectants are inactivated by leftover organic material if used first; Remove dead animals (2 points) -- promptly and away from healthy animals; Isolate sick animals (2 points) -- fed, watered, and handled last, with separate equipment; Two-week quarantine of new animals (1 point) -- treated as potentially diseased until quarantine is complete; and Youth involvement and teaching (1 point) -- involving children and the whole household, since awareness itself is a powerful prevention tool. A total biosecurity score of 1-10 is rated 'poor', 11-20 'moderate', and 21-30 'good'. The tool's design intentionally fits on a single page to keep it simple and practical for smallholder use, and can be applied across multiple livestock species and diseases, not just cattle.
